officials.name: Charles Curran
officials.bio: The son of a railroad construction worker, Charles Curran was born in 1939 in Galion, Ohio, and graduated from Eastern Illinois University in 1963. He served as a Dayton City Commissioner (1970-1979), Ohio State Senator (1979-1983), and Montgomery County Commissioner (1983-2006). Charles brings extensive government experience to his role as Councilmember, having also taught political science at Sinclair Community College until his retirement in 2017.

officials.name: David Litteral
officials.bio: David Litteral was elected to Beavercreek City Council in January 2024, following a distinguished 25-year career as a Greene County Deputy Sheriff where he held various roles including Sergeant and Community Engagement Deputy. A lifelong resident of Greene County, he has called Beavercreek home for 28 years with his wife Melissa. He is dedicated to serving the citizens of the city and making a positive impact on residents' safety and security.

officials.name: Glen Duerr
officials.bio: Glen Duerr was appointed to City Council in April 2020 and then elected to a four-year term in November 2021. He serves as Chair of the Department of History and Government, and Professor of International Studies at Cedarville University.

officials.name: Pete Bales
officials.bio: Councilman Pete Bales is married to Amanda and has two children, Jack and Cara. A lifelong resident of Beavercreek and a 1990 graduate of Beavercreek High School, he earned a Bachelor's of Science degree in Education from The Ohio State University in 1994. Following college, Bales initiated his municipal career with the City of Beavercreek in the Parks, Recreation & Culture Department.

officials.name: Sarah Bills
officials.bio: Sarah Bills was born and raised in Cleveland, Ohio, and earned a degree from Cleveland State University. A Beavercreek resident for 21 years, she is deeply involved in education, family life, and community service, including roles on the Beavercreek Tree Advisory Board and with the Beavercreek Wetlands Association.

officials.name: Don Adams
officials.bio: Don Adams is retired after spending 50 years as a national sales manager in the optical field. He continues to contribute to his community by volunteering through various roles: Neighborhood Assistance Officer at the Dayton Police Department, Vice President of the Jaycees local chapter, District Director, Squadron Commander, and Group Commander for Civil Air Patrol with the Rank of Major, Greater Dayton Emmaus Community Board Chair, Beavercreek High School Choir Department Treasurer, Beavercreek Music Parents Association President, and Beavercreek High School Friends Annual Show Choir’s Stage Manager. Don currently serves as the President of the Beavercreek Police Citizens Police Academy Alumni and Citizens on Preventive Patrol. He is also a member of the Beavercreek Township Fire Department Auxiliary and Citizen Emergency Response Team. In 2014, Don received the Citizen of the Year award from the Miami Valley Crime Stoppers. He holds the position of President at the Wright B Flyer Museum and is a board member of the National Aviation Heritage Area. Furthermore, Don is the President-elect of the Rotary Club of Beavercreek, a member of the Kingswood Forest Board of Directors, an Elder for 11 years at Beavercreek Christian Church, and a Beavercreek City Council member and Vice Mayor. In 2022, Don was honored with the E.G. Shaw Award for Lifetime Achievement by the Beavercreek Chamber of Commerce and was appointed to the Board of the Family Violence Prevention Center. Don and his wife, Ann, have been residents of Beavercreek for 45 years. They are proud parents of three children, grandparents to five grandchildren, and great-grandparents to two great-grandchildren.

officials.name: Zach Upton
officials.bio: Vice Mayor Zach Upton and his wife, Heather, are the proud parents of Ainsley and Reagen. Upton brings a strong background in public service and professional expertise to the Beavercreek City Council. A 2002 graduate and class president of Beavercreek High School, he earned a bachelor’s degree in history and politics from Regent University.

officials.name: James Babcock
officials.bio: James Babcock serves as a Council Person At Large and Assistant Majority Leader. He is a graduate of Central Catholic High School and works as a Realtor. He is involved in several committees and community organizations, with his term expiring December 31, 2027.

officials.name: Brenda Kimbrough
officials.bio: Brenda Kimbrough serves as the Ward 2 Council Person. She holds an Associates Degree in Applied Science in Educational Technology from the University of Akron and is currently an Office Manager at Stark Community Support Network.

officials.name: Chris Smith
officials.bio: Chris Smith serves as the Ward 4 Council Person for Canton, Ohio. She is the owner of Chris' Talk of the Town Beauty Salon and holds a Doctorate Degree from the National Institute of Cosmetology.

officials.name: J. Nate Cooks
officials.bio: J. Nate Cooks serves as the Ward 6 Council Person. He is a graduate of McKinley High School, Gray's Harbor Community College, Walsh College, and Walsh University, holding a Masters in Counseling and Human Development. He is currently employed at Stark State College.

officials.name: Jason Scaglione
officials.bio: Jason Scaglione serves as the Ward 3 Council Person for Canton, Ohio. He chairs the Public Property Capital Improvement Committee and is a member of several other committees, focusing on neighborhood safety and community development.

officials.name: Robert Fisher
officials.bio: Robert Fisher serves as the Ward 5 Council Person. He chairs the Environmental & Public Utilities Committee and is a member of the Public Property Capital Improvement, Judiciary, and Public Safety & Thoroughfares Committees. His current term expires on December 31, 2027.

officials.name: Louis Giavasis
officials.bio: Louis Giavasis serves as the Council President for Canton, Ohio. He is a Democrat and is currently retired, having previously served as Stark County Clerk of Courts and President of the Plain Township Board of Trustees.

officials.name: Anna Albi
officials.bio: Anna (she/her) is a professional communicator and community advocate. As local group lead for Moms Demand Action in Cincinnati, Anna worked with elected officials, law enforcement, and community partners to promote gun safety and work towards solutions that will reduce gun violence. Anna formerly served as recording secretary for Madisonville Community Council, where she focused on connecting residents with City Council to ensure the needs and preferences of the community are prioritized.

officials.name: Evan Nolan
officials.bio: Evan Nolan grew up in Cheviot, Cincinnati, and is a graduate of St. Xavier High School, the University of Pennsylvania, and Georgetown University. He began his career as a public sector consultant for IBM and later served as a legal fellow for U.S. Senator Sherrod Brown. He currently practices transactional and real estate law at Katz Teller Law Firm.

officials.name: Jeff Cramerding
officials.bio: Councilmember Jeff Cramerding was born and raised in Cincinnati. Prior to joining council, he served as legislative aide to Councilmember Todd Portune and has been involved in numerous candidate and issue campaigns in Cincinnati. He built his career as a labor lawyer and currently serves as Director of Contract Administration for the American Association of University Professors at UC. Jeff is an active Price Hill community member and a founding board member of Price Hill Will. He has been a long-time advocate of supporting mixed-income neighborhoods in Cincinnati as the affordable housing crisis becomes more prevalent, and serves as the chair of the Equitable Growth and Housing Committee. Jeff lives in Price Hill with his three children and one terrible cat.

officials.name: Mark Jeffreys
officials.bio: Mark Jeffreys grew up working poor, eventually earning an MBA from Georgetown. He spent 16 years at Procter & Gamble before launching his own startups. He is active in the community, serving on boards and founding the non-profit go Vibrant, and lives in Clifton with his wife and four children.

officials.name: Meeka Owens
officials.bio: Councilmember Meeka D. Owens was elected to City Council in 2021 and chairs the Climate, Environment, and Infrastructure Committee, among other roles. Born and raised in Avondale, she holds a B.S. from Miami University and an M.Ed. from Xavier University. Dedicated to community service, her goals for Cincinnati include increasing safety, creating affordable housing, and fostering a more sustainable city.

officials.name: Scotty Johnson
officials.bio: A Cincinnati native and beloved public servant, Scotty Johnson strives to exude the impact of unity and integrity within our great city. Mr. Johnson graduated from Woodward High School and Bowling Green State University with a Bachelor of Science in Criminal Law, minoring in Psychology. He also attained certification in Race Relations from Harvard University. Having honorably served the Cincinnati Police Department for 33 years, Councilmember Johnson is passionate about achieving quality and impartial service for every citizen of Cincinnati.

officials.name: Seth Walsh
officials.bio: A native of St. Joseph, Michigan, Seth Walsh moved to Cincinnati to attend Xavier University, where he was elected Student Body President. He has worked for various members of Cincinnati City Council and served as Executive Director of the College Hill CURC. In his free time, Seth founded the Cincy Soccer League and serves on the Board of Directors for the Friends of the Taft Family Legacy.

officials.name: Jan-Michele Lemon Kearney
officials.bio: Jan-Michele was born in Cincinnati and is a proud graduate of Cincinnati Public Schools (Rockdale Elementary and Walnut Hills High School). Her father, Dr. Luther J. Lemon, was a family physician for more than 50 years, and her mother, Elizabeth M. Lemon was a CPS teacher. She is honored to serve the residents of the city she loves.

officials.name: Justin M. Bibb
officials.bio: Justin M. Bibb is the 58th Mayor of Cleveland working to improve public safety, invest in neighborhoods and modernize City Hall. On January 3, 2022, Mayor Bibb took the oath of office as the city’s first millennial mayor.

officials.name: Richard Gould
officials.bio: Richard (Dick) Gould is a lifetime resident of the Dayton area. Dick is a certified public accountant and was elected as a Greene County Commissioner in 2023 for a four-year term ending January 2026.

officials.name: Sarah J. Mays
officials.bio: Sarah J. Mays, a lifelong resident of Xenia, Ohio, has dedicated her career to building a stronger Greene County through collaboration and community development. She earned a bachelor’s degree in psychology from Cedarville University and worked in the university’s Development and Advancement Office for seven years.

officials.name: Thomas R. Koogler
officials.bio: Tom Koogler is a life-long resident of Greene County, Ohio, and a successful entrepreneur who founded T.R. Koogler Refuse Collection, later sold to Waste Management, Inc., where he served as a Regional Vice President. He began his third four-year term as Greene County Commissioner in 2021, bringing extensive business experience and a commitment to numerous nonprofit organizations.

officials.name: Dr. Kevin Sharrett
officials.bio: Dr. Kevin Sharrett has served Greene County as Coroner since 1997. Dr. Sharrett is a 1991 graduate of the Wright State University School of Medicine and also has a family practice in Jamestown.

officials.name: Adolfo A. Tornichio
officials.bio: Judge Adolfo Tornichio was raised in Greene County, Ohio, and earned a Bachelor of Arts in political science from Wright State University. He graduated from the University of Toledo College of Law in 1998 with a Juris Doctorate and began his legal career as an Assistant Prosecuting Attorney for Greene County.

officials.name: Michael A. Buckwalter
officials.bio: Judge Michael Buckwalter was born and raised in Greene County, Ohio, graduating from Xenia High School in 1975, Wright State University in 1981, and the University of Dayton School of Law in 1984. While in law school, he clerked for several judges in Greene County Common Pleas Court and was selected to the National Moot Court Team. He now serves as Greene County Common Pleas Court Senior Judge and is the current Presiding Judge.

officials.name: Cynthia Martin
officials.bio: Judge Cynthia Martin began her judicial career as Domestic Relations Court Magistrate in 2006, serving as Chief Magistrate from 2014-2020 before being elected Judge in 2021. She earned her law degree from the University of Dayton, School of Law in 1992, and previously worked as a solo practitioner focusing on family law and as an attorney for Ohio's Attorney General.

officials.name: John T. Plecnik
officials.bio: Commissioner John Plecnik was sworn in as the 79th Commissioner of Lake County, Ohio, on February 11, 2021, and for his second term on December 29, 2022. He is one of three Lake County Commissioners, responsible for setting the budget and administrative policy for county government. He previously served as Vice President of Council for the City of Willoughby Hills and holds degrees in accounting, law, and tax.

officials.name: Morgan R. McIntosh
officials.bio: Morgan R. McIntosh was appointed Lake County Commissioner on January 6, 2026. Prior to this, he served as President of AMFM Incorporated for 20 years. He earned a BS in law enforcement from Minnesota State University and had a brief career as a police officer.

officials.name: Morris Beverage III
officials.bio: Morris Beverage III is a lifelong, third-generation resident of Lake County, serving as a Lake County Commissioner. He brings both business experience and a passion for public service to his role, shaped by his deep commitment to serving the community where he was born and raised.

officials.name: Kristin Saban
officials.bio: Clerk of Council Kristin Saban served nearly seven years as Ward 4 councilwoman. She also worked as the chief of staff to Mayor Anthony Biasiotta in the City of Seven Hills before taking on her new role. Saban was born and raised in Parma, a 1994 graduate of Parma Senior High School, and attended Cuyahoga Community College's Western Campus.

officials.name: Kammy Coyle Shuman
officials.bio: Councilwoman Kammy Coyle Shuman is a longtime resident of Parma. She graduated from Padua Franciscan High School in Parma and then earned a bachelor's degree in accounting from Baldwin Wallace University. She is currently the operations manager at Oak Tree Wealth Partners in Independence, Ohio.

officials.name: Deborah Lime
officials.office: City Council Member, President Pro Tempore
officials.bio: Councilwoman Deborah Lime has been a resident of Ward 2 for more than 50 years and serves on several committees including Finance and Public Safety (Chairwoman). She previously served as Ward 2 councilwoman from 1991-2003 and again from 2011. Deborah and her husband, Mark, have four children and two grandchildren.

officials.name: Allan Divis
officials.bio: Councilman Allan Divis was elected to serve the residents of Ward 5 in November 2011. He is a Cleveland native with an associate degree in business and has been involved with coaching and serving St. Anthony Parish programs. He and his wife, Michele, have four children.

officials.name: Amanda Boyd
officials.bio: Amanda Boyd began her term as Ward 8 councilwoman in January 2024. Previously, she served for five years on the City of Parma's Board of Building Appeals and for six years on the Executive Cuyahoga County Central Committee. She also worked with students in the drama program at Parma Senior High School from 2018 to 2020.

officials.name: John Soeder
officials.bio: Committees: Finance, Governmental Operations (Vice Chairman), Public Service, Environmental Standards, Public Housing, Appointment Scanning.

officials.name: Kelly Zacharias
officials.bio: Committees: Finance, Governmental Operations, Planning, Public Safety, Environmental Standards (Chairwoman), Public Housing.

officials.name: Kevin Kussmaul
officials.bio: Ward 6 Councilman Kevin Kussmaul was born and raised in Parma, graduating from Normandy High School in 2012. He earned both a bachelor's and master's degree in business administration from John Carroll University. Kussmaul currently works as a strategic accounts program manager and has been a member of the Parma Area Chamber of Commerce and Young Professionals of Parma.

officials.name: Monica Wilson
officials.bio: Monica Wilson began her service on Parma City Council representing Ward 1 in early 2023. She is a 30+ year resident of Parma, originally from Detroit, Michigan. Wilson's professional background spans more than three decades in the paints and coating industry, where she worked in senior global management roles.

officials.name: Vito Dipierro
officials.bio: In January 2023, Vito Dipierro began serving as council president, having previously served as Ward 1 councilman since November 2013. The son of Italian immigrants, he graduated from Normandy High School in 1995 and later earned his real estate license in 2002, starting his own brokerage in 2013.

officials.name: Cliff Mears
officials.bio: Cliff Mears holds a Bachelor of Arts in Communications and has a diverse professional background in industrial relations, finance, and communications, including roles at National Geographic Society. He taught Communications for over 20 years and served on the Mansfield Playhouse Board. Prior to becoming County Commissioner, he was President of Mansfield City Council.

officials.name: Darrell Banks
officials.bio: Darrell Banks has served as Richland County Commissioner, following nine years as Mayor of the Village of Bellville. He previously owned and operated several businesses in Richland County for over 25 years and also taught vocational education. Darrell has been an industry leader, serving as president of the Ohio Restaurant Association and co-founder of the Richland County Convention and Visitors Bureau.

officials.name: Tony Vero
officials.bio: Anthony “Tony” Vero was born and raised in Canton, Ohio, and took permanent residence in Richland County in the fall of 2004. He graduated from Miami University and the University of Akron School of Law, and is licensed to practice law in Ohio. Prior to becoming commissioner on January 3, 2017, Tony worked in the private sector and served on the Village of Lexington Council.

officials.bio: Ilene Shapiro, Summit County Executive, focuses on fostering innovation and economic competitiveness. She collaborates with partners to make Summit County an ideal place to live and work, highlighting its vibrant city, communities, a research university, and a national park.

officials.bio: Wade Kapszukiewicz was elected mayor of Toledo, Ohio on November 7, 2017, becoming the 64th mayor of the city. He was re-elected for a historic third term on November 4, 2025. During his tenure, he has focused on creating a regional water system, increasing the police force, and restoring the city's budget.

officials.name: Donald E. Oda
officials.office: Common Pleas Court General Division Judge
officials.bio: Judge Donald E. Oda II earned his Juris Doctor in 1995 and began a general law practice in Warren County, Ohio. He was elected to the Warren County Court in 2004 and later to the Warren County Common Pleas Court in 2012, where he is currently the longest-serving judge. He resides in Clearcreek Township with his wife, Linda Oda, and they have two children and three grandchildren.

officials.name: Robert Peeler
officials.office: Common Pleas Court General Division Judge
officials.bio: Judge Robert Peeler is an active duty veteran of the United States Army. He obtained a Bachelor of Science in Business Management from Murray State University and received his Juris Doctorate from Chase College of Law where he served on the National Moot Court team and was President of the Student Bar Association. He served as an Extern in the office of the United States Attorney, Special Prosecutor’s Unit, White Collar Crime division from 1981-1982.

officials.name: Timothy N. Tepe
officials.office: Common Pleas Court General Division Judge
officials.bio: Judge Tepe is a graduate of Moeller High School, The University of Dayton and The University of Dayton School of Law. As a practicing trial attorney, he maintained his law practice in Warren County for 31 years before taking the bench in 2017. From 2005- 2016, he served as the prosecuting attorney for the City of Springboro.

officials.name: Russell L. Uptegrove
officials.hours: Monday - Thursday 9:00AM to 4:00PM (except Holidays )(hours may vary)
officials.bio: Dr. Uptegrove started with the Coroner's Office in April 2004 and was appointed County Coroner in April 2007. He received his medical degree from the Medical University of South Carolina and completed a fellowship in Forensic Pathology. He also serves as a Forensic Pathologist for the Montgomery County Coroner's Office.

officials.name: Gary Loxley
officials.bio: Judge Loxley has served as a judge on the Warren County Court since May 2013. A native of Greenville, Ohio, Judge Loxley began his legal career as an officer in the United States Army Judge Advocate General’s Corps in 1988. In 2015, he established the Warren County Veterans Court and serves as its Presiding Judge.

officials.name: Joseph W. Kirby
officials.bio: Judge Kirby graduated from the Salmon P. Chase College of Law with a Juris-Doctorate degree and was admitted to the practice of law before the Ohio Supreme Court in November 1995. Prior to taking the bench, Judge Kirby was a partner in a family law firm in Springboro, Ohio whose practice consisted primarily of criminal defense, personal injury and family law.
